2011_028_100411regmtg.paragraph: Board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of October 4, 2011, combining student recognitions, the September 6 and September 20 minutes, the August 2011 Treasurer's Report and check register, and business items on copy paper, network and storage purchases, three teacher hires, professional development and a new educator appraisal model. Its most consequential content is Mark S. Rajter's legislative report: the state foundation allowance fell from $9,275 per student in FY 2010-2011 to $8,805 in FY 2011-2012, a permanent reduction of ($470) that the presentation shows against an estimated 12,096 students as a permanent loss of revenue of ($5,685,000).

**Meeting.** Troy Board of Education regular meeting, October 4, 2011, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW).

**Recognitions.** Student representatives Jonny Dowdall (Athens High) and Maggie Steele (Troy High); more than 350 students honored for Advanced Placement exam performance with eight National AP Scholars invited; fifty-two (52) National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists, to be honored at a November 9 reception; and the Nicholas Green Distinguished Student Award, carrying a $500 U.S. savings bond, to Brittany Ngia of Boulan Park Middle School, presented by Elizabeth Brooks.

**September 6, 2011 minutes.** Resolutions 11-086 through 11-091 all passed Ayes 7 / Nays 0: memorializing Anthony Spagnola, a Board member from July 1991 through June 2007; approving August 16 minutes; approving 13 new hires; entering a Service Consolidation Plan agreement with MDE under MCL 388.1622f(1)(c) to qualify for the $100 per pupil Best Practices incentive; certifying Edmunds, Fleming and Miletti as MASB Delegate Assembly delegates for October 27, 2011; and adopting committee memberships. Ida Edmunds received the MASB President's Award for seven certification levels and 1,383 credits, one of only 59 statewide, after service since 1985; the district won the ASBO Certificate of Excellence for the 22nd straight year for the CAFR for the year ended June 30, 2010. Enrollment rose approximately 300 pupils, elementary up 137 on an increase of only 2.0 FTE and middle school up 52. Adjourned 8:37 p.m.

**Identification.** Troy School District (Troy, Michigan) Board of Education regular meeting packet, October 4, 2011, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August.

**Recognitions.** Student representatives Jonny Dowdall, an Athens High School senior and Oakland Astronomy Club member, and Maggie Steele, a Troy High School junior. More than 350 Troy students were honored for Advanced Placement exam performance; the National AP Scholars invited, who earned the honor in their junior year with an average grade of four across eight or more exams, were Sandeep Arakali, David Bai, Neha Bokil, Allen Chen, Rolland He, Darwin Hsu, Yujing Liang and Clark Zhang. Troy had fifty-two (52) National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists, drawn from more than one million entrants at some 22,000 high schools nationwide of whom 16,000 were selected, requiring scores in the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT; the resolution was signed the fourth day of October, 2011, with a reception November 9. The Nicholas Green Distinguished Student Award of the National Association for Gifted Children, honoring the Greens' seven-year-old son Nicholas killed in a drive-by shooting in Italy in 1994, went to Brittany Ngia, a sixth grader at Boulan Park Middle School and daughter of Lester Ngia and Natalie Lee, nominated by Suzanne Miller of Hamilton Elementary; the award carries a $500 U.S. savings bond and goes to one child per state per year in grades 3 through 6. Presenter Elizabeth Brooks is a retired Grand Blanc Community Schools teacher and chair of the MAGC scholarship committee.

**Minutes, September 6, 2011.** Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Malven, Miletti and Underwood present, Superintendent Fowler, administrators Birmingham, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter, Stromayer and Witt, and approximately 28 audience members. Fifteen spring-sport All-State athletes were recognized. MASB Executive Director Kathy Hayes drove 100 miles to present Ida Edmunds the President's Award of Recognition for all seven levels of certification and 1,383 certification credits, one of only 59 in the state; Edmunds has served since 1985. The district earned the ASBO International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the 22nd straight year, for the CAFR for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2010; a plaque went to Mark Rajter, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services. Resolution 11-086 honored Anthony Spagnola, born in Easton, Pennsylvania on May 20, 1950 and deceased July 20, 2011 at age 61, a Board member from July 1991 through June 2007, 16 years including several as president; the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence renamed its golf event the Tony Spagnola Invitational Golf Outing. Recess 7:26 p.m., reconvened 7:31 p.m. Resolution 11-087 approved the August 16, 2011 minutes; 11-088 approved 13 new hires including Sara Ballinger, Julie Eldridge, Ashley Falzon, Eric Flessa, Lisa Gaglio, Amanda Hazergian, Emily Louks, Rhiannon Mitchell, Melven Moffett, Jeanine Pica, Christopher Rich, Cheryl Rowley and Rita Suleyman. Bob Stromayer reported on summer 2011 programs with no tuition increase, a slide showing a 4% increase in numbers since last year, and Dr. Machesky's new Summer Success Academy for select 9th graders. Larson and Athens did not meet AYP because of subgroups with more than 30 students. Enrollment as of September 6, 2011: elementary up 137 supported by an increase of only 2.0 FTE, middle school up 52, overall increase of approximately 300 pupils. Resolution 11-089 entered a Service Consolidation Plan agreement with the Michigan Department of Education under MCL 388.1622f(1)(c) and MDE guidance distributed June 30, 2011, to qualify for the $100 per pupil Best Practices incentive. Resolution 11-090 certified Ida Edmunds, Paula Fleming and Todd Miletti as delegates to the MASB 2011 Delegate Assembly on October 27, 2011; 11-091 adopted 2011/2012 committee memberships. All votes were Ayes 7, Nays 0. Adjourned 8:37 p.m., minutes by Paula Fleming, Secretary. The September 20, 2011 workshop ran 6:00 p.m. to 9:50 p.m. on MME results and Common Core, staffing and Schools of Choice, and legislative updates.

**Item 5.D, copy paper bid #9719.** Memorandum of September 14, 2011 from Sara L. Konieczka, Purchasing Supervisor (1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, 248-823-4052). Bids opened September 13, 2011 for white high-speed xerographic paper, 8 1/2 x 11, 20#, 92 brightness, 500 sheets per ream, 10 reams per case, total quantity 2,520 cases; bids were sent to seven potential bidders with 9 responding. Award recommended to current provider Contract Paper Group at unit price 25.32 for $63,806.40, ahead of Midland Paper 25.7895/$64,989.54, Global Office Solutions 26.85/$67,662.00, Paper Express 27.55/$69,426.00, Xerox 27.99/$70,534.80, National Packaging Corp 28.50/$71,820.00, Accurate Forms & Supplies 28.59/$72,046.80, Quill 29.90/$75,348.00 and Office Supply Giant.com 36.53/$92,055.60; Office Depot, Amerisource and Office Express did not respond. Expenditure of the 2011-12 General Fund.

**Item 6.A, personnel.** Probationary 2011/2012 contracts recommended for Elizabeth Crawford, 1.0 FTE AM/PM kindergarten at Morse Elementary (B.S. Central Michigan University May 2011, Michigan provisional certificate June 2011, of Rochester Hills); Noah Elkins, 1.0 FTE French at Athens High School (B.A. Western Michigan University December 2009, provisional certificate February 2011, of Sterling Heights); and Lauren Gardner, .5 FTE chemistry at International Academy East (B.S. Oakland University April 2011, provisional certificate June 2011, of Auburn Hills).

**Item 7.A, Sex Education Advisory Board 2011-2012.** At least one-half of the board must be parents and one parent must co-chair. Co-chairs Larry Hahn, principal of Baker Middle School, and parent Nicole Jenkins. Members include teachers Mary McDermott (Troy High) and Kevin Wilson (Boulan Park), Rev. Jack Mannschreck of Big Beaver United Methodist Church, nurse Lois Winer of the Oakland Health Department, parents Debbie Liposky, Linda Robertson, Cheryl Webster-Miller, Ann O'Neill, Cherie Armstrong and Mary Kafarski, resident Diane Trombley, and students Sandy Mouch (AHS 2012) and Dejan Jenkins (THS 2014). Updated 9-22-11.

**Item 7.B, professional development.** Presented by Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment. Topics: SIOP and its eight components; an administrative retreat; new principals David Pass, Matt Jansen, Anthony Morse and Stephanie Acord at Troy Union, Wass, Boulan Park and Morse; a new-teacher roster with the figure 27 adjacent; the eight Standards of Mathematical Practice; Holt McDougal MS ELA; Atlas Rubicon; Inform; data meetings; a middle school social studies adoption cycle grid spanning 2011-2012 through 2017-2018; a Diversity and Inclusion Council; and after-school sessions themed on Educational Leadership on September 26 (KALPA 381872), November 7 (KALPA 381878), March 26 (KALPA 381879) and April 30 (KALPA 381880). North Central Accreditation work includes monthly newsletters, four new district SMART goals, parent, student and staff surveys in November, and a Student Learning Showcase on May 17, 2012 in the Services Board Room, 12:30 to 3:30. Current Title 1 buildings are Troy Union, Wattles, Costello (new), Barnard, Baker and Larson (new); Morse, Wass, Smith and Hill were discontinued.

**Item 7.C, Troy Educator Appraisal Model.** Presented by Dr. Rich Machesky and Karen Bush. A committee of eight TEA members and eight administrators formed in the second semester of 2010-2011 created the instrument to comply with Michigan education reform legislation; the attached proposed plan is dated August 2011 with a footer of Monday, August 29, 2011. Four performance levels crosswalk to state ratings: Unsatisfactory to Unsatisfactory, Gaining Proficiency to Minimally Effective, Proficient to Effective, Exceeds Proficiency to Highly Effective. Three tracks (Track 1 probationary, Track II A and Track II B) and five domains: planning and preparation, classroom environment, instruction, professional responsibilities, and demonstrating student growth. Four district goals cover literacy, mathematics, science and social studies.

**Item 8.A, network core.** Memorandum of September 28, 2011 from Merri Lynn Colligan, Director of Technology (Technology Resource Center, 4420 Livernois, 248/823-5090) to Dr. Fowler. The district is moving to centralized servers and the Troy Cloud and must upgrade core router connections from 1 Gig to 10 Gig; the two existing 6509 core routers have no redundancy. Recommended purchase of 2 Cisco Nexus 5010 units and two 6509 Supervisor 720 cards with 2 10 Gig ports, priced against REMC, MICTA, AEPA and Oakland County cooperative bids. Resolution awards the bid to Netech in the amount of $105,388.50 as an expenditure of the 2004 Capital Projects Fund, described as a Bond Fund expenditure. The NETech quote from Scott Sutherland includes supervisors at $41,800.00, chassis at $9,487.50 each, storage protocol licenses at $6,600.00 each, X2-10GB-SR modules $4,389.00, 52 hours of labor for $8,060.00 and a trade-in of the current Sup 720s at ($7,320.00); valid 30 days.

**Item 8.B, storage and backup.** The Network Area Storage purchased in 2004 has passed the five-year useful life of a storage server. The department consulted the Oakland ISD Technology Department about a fee-for-service option, but the cost was prohibitive and the ISD did not have the requested disk space. After demos of Dell Compellent and EMC, EMC was preferred for scaling to support up to 4000 virtual desktops in the Troy Cloud. Recommended purchase of an EMC VMAXe and an EMC Avamar backup server. The resolution as printed awards the bid to CDWg in the amount of $636,000.00 as an expenditure of the 2004 Capital Projects Fund, though its text repeats the phrase network core. The CDW quote of September 23, 2011 (customer #4541043, account manager Eric Christensen, prepared by Jerome Cheng) lists 24 2000GB drives, 72 450GB 15K drives, 12 200GB flash drives and three Avamar Gen4 3.9TB storage nodes; VMAXe subtotal and grand total $636,000.00 with Avamar included and freight $0.00, under contract AEPA Michigan.

**Item 8.C, legislative impact on school funding.** Presented by Mark S. Rajter, October 4, 2011; no action required. Foundation allowance FY 2010-2011 $9,275 per student; permanent reduction ($470) per student; foundation allowance FY 2011-2012 $8,805 per student. An estimated student count of 12,096 against the ($470) reduction is shown as a permanent loss of revenue of ($5,685,000). One-time 2011/2012 adjustments offsetting the $470 per pupil reduction are $100 per pupil toward MPSERS costs of approximately $230 per pupil and $100 per pupil for adopting four of five best practices: charging employees at least 10% of health care premiums, being policy holder of employee medical benefit plans, developing a service consolidation plan, obtaining competitive bids on non-instructional services, and providing a dashboard or report card. Proposed personal property tax elimination would directly cost hold harmless millage $1,449,321 and debt millage $1,352,059, with indirect ISD funding impact of ($12.7 million): general fund $758,000; special education P.A. 18 revenue $9,649,000, of which TSD's 5.5% share is ($530,000); vocational education $2,316,000.

**Item 11.A, closed session.** Resolution to enter closed session on an attorney-client privilege item as permitted by the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), by roll call of Philippart, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Malven and Miletti; no votes are recorded in the packet and no additional business would follow other than adjournment.
